problem: Suppose $C$ is a $9\times 9$ matrix and $det(C)=-69.$ The matrix $D$ is obtained from $C$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{5}↔{R}_{8}$ (switching the fifth and the eighth rows). What is the value of $det(D)?$
worked_solution:
Since swapping any two rows changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite sign, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(D) & =-det(C) \\  & =-(-69) \\  & =69.\end{aligned}
$$
